cutoff_window.qualification_rule: Only public sources with direct visible dates inside the strict two-day window were included. Date-only September 5 items were accepted only when the visible page also showed a release or publication context inside the window; older, missing-date, ambiguous, future-dated, or snippet-only dates were excluded.

federation_boundary.local_owner_scope: AI-assisted development practice: context architecture, source workflows, instructions, agent workflows, coding practices, retrieval and tools, verification/evals, application patterns, governance/risk, and adoption/operating model.
federation_boundary.collector_action: Recorded practice implications and routing notes only; did not update docs/wiki or raw/processed.

qualifying_updates.title: OpenAI shares internal coding-agent adoption and measurement snapshot
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: OpenAI reported that researchers now use coding agents throughout the day, often concurrently, and that research organization agent runtime reached 3.1 agent workdays for every human workday by mid-August. The post also describes a six-phase taxonomy for classifying agent work and notes that successful 4-8 hour tasks often still require one or more human interventions.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The local practice signal is that agent adoption should be measured by workflow taxonomies, intervention rates, and task horizon, not just raw usage or generated-code volume.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Candidate coverage for agent operating metrics, concurrent session norms, and human-steering thresholds in high-complexity coding-agent workflows.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Ingest should avoid creating an OpenAI entity page locally; preserve only measurement and operating-model lessons.

qualifying_updates.title: OpenAI describes Codex context preservation and asynchronous question handling with Astra
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: OpenAI's Astra announcement says Codex will preserve notes across context windows, keep earlier context windows searchable, ask asynchronous questions while continuing independent work, and lean into verification through browser testing and code execution during higher-effort coding tasks. The same page says Astra meets OpenAI's Critical cybersecurity threshold and needs stronger safeguards.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The practice update is about context externalization, async human-decision gates, and risk-tiered safeguards for more capable coding agents.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Candidate coverage for persistent context notes, searchable prior windows, async blocking-question queues, and stronger authorization for cyber-capable model use.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Treat product and model facts as upstream-owned; local wiki should keep the context-management and governance lens.

qualifying_updates.title: OpenClaw release adds recovery, swarm, session-access, and MCP operations controls
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: OpenClaw v2026.9.2 highlights reply recovery across gateway restarts, live settings changes, default-enabled swarm orchestration with opt-outs and tool restrictions, cross-agent session visibility controls, Slack approval/session status, personal connected accounts, Gateway latency diagnostics, MCP server failure counts, OAuth sign-in from the MCP servers tab, and isolation for per-client MCP server behavior.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The release shows agent harnesses adding durable recovery, explicit cross-agent visibility scopes, observable MCP health, and operational diagnostics as first-class controls.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Candidate coverage for session recovery, multi-agent visibility policy, MCP degradation handling, and gateway-level telemetry in application harness patterns.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Route OpenClaw product details upstream; local ingest can cite the release as evidence for operational control patterns.

qualifying_updates.title: Kiro Crew release formalizes fleet policy, MCP governance, approvals, and peer-agent steering
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Kiro Crew v0.5.0 adds centrally published security policies, enterprise MCP registry controls with version pins, tamper-evident audit log fixes under concurrent writers, repository-bound app execution trust, changed approval behavior for silent commands and structured tools, bulk and per-call approval handling, readable command digests, agent-to-agent session_send, conductor-managed fan-outs, workflow libraries, wake-on-change PR watches, and model downgrade visibility.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The release is strong practice evidence that coding-agent fleets need centrally distributed policy, provenance-bound tool trust, auditable concurrent writes, and explicit conductor/workflow governance.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Candidate coverage for fleet security policy, approval ergonomics, peer-agent coordination, workflow libraries, and agent audit-chain integrity.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Do not duplicate Kiro Crew product coverage; keep local lens on governance and operating controls.

qualifying_updates.title: Pi release exposes agent runtime compatibility and prompt-cache fixes
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Pi v0.85.1 adds GPT-6 Astra support for OpenAI API keys and OpenAI Codex subscriptions, fixes SDK import failures caused by unintentionally published experimental code and dependencies, and adjusts long prompt-cache requests for GPT-5.6+ Responses models to use a 30-minute prompt cache option.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The local practice signal is that agent CLIs need stable supported SDK surfaces, clear separation of source-only experimental APIs, and cache settings that match provider behavior.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Candidate coverage for provider-compatibility checks, cache-retention tuning, and supported-versus-experimental API boundaries in agent harnesses.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Use cautiously during ingest because this is narrower than the OpenClaw/Kiro governance evidence.

qualifying_updates.title: GrowthOS frames agent experience as task completion, not human web traffic
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GrowthOS listed new agent-user posts dated September 5-7, including agent experience, agent funnels, task-completion rate, silent failures, and traffic metrics that fail to capture zero-click answers, API-mediated demand, and agent-run journeys.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The practice update is a measurement shift: AI-assisted development teams building public docs, APIs, or developer surfaces may need to test whether agents can discover, authenticate, complete, and report on tasks.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Candidate coverage for agent-facing product-surface evals, source citation journeys, docs discoverability, and task-completion funnels.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: If ingested, treat AX terminology as a local evaluation lens rather than a product page.

qualifying_updates.title: Aibl.to publishes team AI adoption guidance centered on real work
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Aibl.to's September 6 blog listing says many companies no longer have an AI access problem, but struggle to turn access into useful behavior; it recommends starting with real work rather than generic tool adoption.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: This supports local operating-model guidance that adoption work should begin from repeatable workflows and behavior changes, not broad tool rollouts.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Candidate coverage for workflow-first AI adoption, training scoping, and practice selection before model or tool standardization.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: The source is a blog index with a visible publication date; ingest should fetch the individual post if available before durable synthesis.

qualifying_updates.title: Hmmnm posts prompt-injection defense framing for AI systems
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Hmmnm's blog index lists a September 5 AI Security post comparing prompt injection to SQL injection and promising a defense playbook with real examples.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Prompt injection remains a core local governance topic for agents that read untrusted tool, retrieval, and web content.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Candidate coverage for prompt-injection defenses around tool results, retrieval context, and agent permissions.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Before ingest, open the article body and verify concrete defense guidance; the collector captured only index-level visible summary.

qualifying_updates.title: MCPMarket daily list surfaces verification, gateway, docs-ingest, and memory MCP patterns
qualifying_updates.visible_date: September 5, 2026 in URL and page title
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The September 5 MCPMarket list ranks servers for binary-claim verification, local MCP gateway consolidation, AI-writing factual checks, documentation scraping for LLM ingestion, headless validation for game development, semantic shared memory, and Git-preserved development decisions.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Although individual MCP servers are upstream-owned, the local practice signal is that MCP ecosystems are converging on verification, provenance, context compression, docs ingestion, and persistent memory patterns.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Candidate coverage for MCP governance checklists, tool-verification patterns, and context-memory surfaces rather than individual server catalog pages.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Route server-specific background upstream; local ingest should extract only pattern-level implications.

qualifying_updates.title: AI Agent Store weekly page highlights incident logs and critical-risk agent safeguards
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: AI Agent Store's September 6 weekly page summarizes public reporting on AI agent misalignment incidents, critical cybersecurity risk classification, and recommends internal misalignment incident logs, escalation paths, threat models, access controls, usage monitoring, and audit trails for agentic systems.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: This is a practice-level governance signal for agent incident reporting and risk-tiered deployment controls, especially when agents can communicate externally or touch security-sensitive systems.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Candidate coverage for incident logs, escalation paths, access monitoring, and procurement questions for high-risk agent workflows.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Prefer primary incident sources during ingest; use this source as a dated routing pointer if primary pages are not directly available.
